topic: The 'healthy' probiotic drinks may be altering your native microbiome
subject: health

facts.claim: Probiotics did not markedly alter the core gut microbiome or detectably colonize the gut environment of Arctic char after a 4-week treatment.
facts.quote: However, they neither markedly altered the core gut microbiome, which was dominated by three bacterial species, nor detectably colonized the gut environment after the 4-week probiotic treatment.

facts.claim: Feeding Lactobacillus casei can have significant impact on the infant microbiome.
facts.quote: There are data that feeding Lactobacillus casei can have significant impact on the infant microbiome [20], but these changes have not yet been linked to health outcomes.

facts.claim: Probiotics utilize competitive exclusion and immunomodulatory mechanisms to reverse parasitic colonization in poultry.
facts.quote: this review uniquely explains how probiotics utilize competitive exclusion and immunomodulatory mechanisms to reverse parasitic colonization.

facts.claim: The application of probiotic consortia changes the imbalance of micro-ecology to the state of relative health and reducing plant mortality.
facts.quote: The application of probiotic consortia changes the imbalance of micro-ecology to the state of relative health and reducing plant mortality.

research.angle: While probiotics can impact the microbiome and utilize competitive exclusion, they may not always result in long-term colonization or significant alterations to core microbial communities.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that probiotic effects are highly variable, with some studies showing significant impacts on infant microbiomes while others show no detectable colonization or core microbiome alteration in fish.
research.caveat: Most research is still in its infancy and many findings have not yet been linked to specific health outcomes.
